To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new class of SEDDS by high throughput screening of SFN and its application in solubilizing poorly soluble drugs and the stability of the SFN-SEDDS was confirmed by microscopic analysis, DSC, FTIR and dissolution study.
a new approach to formulation of SEDDS was introduced utilizing sulforaphane as solubilizer and a high throughput screening approach was introduced for formulation development and stability studies.
a novel class of sulforophane-enabled self-emuslifying drug delivery systems was developed and successfully applied in the formulation and stability studies of poorly water-soluble drug curcumin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class (SFN-SEDSS) of SEDDS by high throughput screening.
the development of a new class SFN-SEDDS formulations for the poorly water soluble drugs.
the development of a new formulation strategy to enhance the bioavailability of poorly soluble drugs by utilizing SFN as a solubilizing agent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study introduced a new class of SEDDS by using SFN as common excipient for solubility enhancement of a set of poorly water soluble model drugs.
the SFN-SEDDS formulation of Curcumin has the potential to improve the oral bioavailability of the poorly water soluble curcumin.
this study introduced a new class of SEDDS by the solubilization capacity of SFN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SFN can be used as a solubilizing agent for the development of SEDDS for poorly water soluble drugs and that high throughput screening is a useful tool for the selection of efficient surfactants/co-surfactants and the development of stable SEDDS.

SFN can be utilized as a solubilizing agent to develop SEDDS for poorly water-soluble drugs and the high throughput screening method is an efficient approach to formulate SEDDs and assess their physical stability.

SFN can be used as a common solubilizing agent for the development of SEDDS of a wide spectrum of poorly water soluble compounds and that the high throughput screening method is an efficient approach in the development of SDDs and stability testing of the formulated SEDDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SEDDS can be successfully developed by utilizing the solvation properties of SFN as common solvent, thus reducing the need for multiple screening of surfactants and/or co-surfactant.
SFN can be used as a novel solubilizer to form self-emulsifying systems of poorly water soluble compounds.
SFN is a novel and efficient solubilizer for SEDDS formulation of poorly water-soluble drugs.
